source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-7: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 7 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Begin with read-only evidence collection and layer isolation; do not change Dynamo configuration until the failure boundary is established. Assume only a multi-node inference service with NVIDIA Dynamo-like frontend, prefill, and decode roles; verify every platform-specific capability rather than inferring it. This is variant 7. Inventory model/runtime revisions, GPU and NIC types, RDMA provider, PCIe/NUMA placement, topology and failure domains, memory limits, deployment configuration, request prompt/output distributions, concurrency, batching, cache state, and tenant policy. Mark missing inventory as evidence_required.

Define the request lifecycle: frontend admission and routing select compatible prefill/decode workers; prefill produces KV with an explicit model, tokenizer, layer, head, position, dtype, and revision schema; decode consumes it only after compatibility, checksum, epoch/lease, namespace, authorization, and tenant-isolation checks. Specify KV movement format and ownership, transport and serialization costs, placement/replication, queueing and scheduling policy, admission quotas/backpressure, expiry/eviction, and control-plane commit states. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, incompatible, or unauthorized state instead of silently using it. For RDMA timeout, congestion, link/NIC failure, worker loss, queue overload, or control-plane inconsistency, use bounded retries and deadlines, fence the failed owner, preserve request correctness, and fall back to recomputation or conventional serving. Define rollback/canary gates for error rate, output-integrity failures, fallback rate, or p99 latency; retain an operational audit trail.

Falsifiable hypothesis: under a declared workload and SLO, Dynamo orchestration lowers TTFT and end-to-end p95/p99 latency or raises useful tokens/s versus matched single-node/local-KV and conventional distributed baselines, without changing model outputs. Measure requests/s and tokens/s, TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency (p50/p95/p99 in ms), queue wait, prefill/decode service time, KV hit/miss and bytes, serialization/copy time, RDMA operations/bytes/timeouts, network and GPU/NIC utilization, memory, retries, fallbacks, errors, and output equivalence. Run repeated randomized trials with fixed model/runtime revisions, matched offered load, warm and cold cache conditions, declared warm-up, confidence intervals, and failure injection. Attribute transport separately from PCIe/NUMA copies, scheduling, queueing, prefill, decode, and control-plane work; report topology, link utilization, replication/compression, competing traffic, and thermal/resource contention. Do not claim improvement until these measurements, compatibility checks, observability coverage, and recovery evidence are available.
risks: unverified Dynamo, RDMA, model-compatibility, and topology assumptions
remote KV or orchestration can worsen tail latency or compromise correctness if state is stale, corrupt, or unauthorized
synthetic failure-injection and benchmark results may not generalize to production traffic
evidence_required: versioned model/runtime/Dynamo configuration and GPU/NIC/RDMA/topology inventory
matched local-KV and conventional distributed-serving benchmark results with units, repetitions, and cache-state controls
stage-level latency, queueing, KV-transfer, utilization, correctness, and tail measurements
authorization, tenant isolation, integrity validation, observability, rollback, and node/link/control-plane failure evidence
